components.title: Session sign-in proxy
components.description: oauth2-proxy in front of each workspace session.

control-implementations.description: What the session sidecar's configuration, rendered from the Theia Cloud releases with the CI site file, shows.

implemented-requirements.description: The session sidecar verifies TLS to Keycloak.

statements.description: The session sidecar's rendered configuration keeps TLS verification on (ssl_insecure_skip_verify=false) and, for its sign-in provider, trusts only the site CA file, not the system trust store, when it reaches the site realm's issuer over HTTPS.
statements.remarks: Your organization operates the site PKI whose chain the sidecar trusts.

implemented-requirements.description: The session sidecar's cookie is protected.

statements.description: The session sidecar sets its session cookie Secure and reads the cookie secret from a file mounted from Secret oauth2-proxy-secrets, never from its configuration; neither of the Theia Cloud chart's public sample secrets appears in any rendered Theia Cloud release.
statements.remarks: Your organization's install writes the site's own cookie secret.

implemented-requirements.description: The session sidecar uses the site's own client secret.

statements.description: The session sidecar reads its sign-in client secret from a file mounted from Secret oauth2-proxy-secrets, the Theia Cloud service reads the same client secret from that Secret, and no rendered Theia Cloud release holds the chart's public sample secrets.
statements.remarks: Your organization's install writes the site's own client secret, matching the realm's confidential session client.

implemented-requirements.description: The session sidecar signs the person in and forwards who they are.

statements.description: The session sidecar signs people in against the site realm and forwards the access token, the user and the email from the token's claims in X-Forwarded-Access-Token, X-Auth-Request-User and X-Auth-Request-Email, replacing any value the request carried; the only sign-in parameters it passes on are a numeric max_age, the site's step-up acr value and prompt=login. It trusts forwarded addresses only from the site's pod range, and the render stops when that range is missing or open to every address; a network policy lets only HAProxy reach the sidecar's port and only the operator reach the workbench's port.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the site's cluster ranges in the site file.
